text:
Zach Whitecloud scored his first goal as a Flame last Sunday against Philadelphia, ten months after Calgary got him from Vegas in the January trade that sent Rasmus Andersson the other way. The goal was a footnote to his real job. The 2023 Cup winner is a minutes-eater on a rebuilding blue line, over 20 a night, with 37 blocked shots and 33 hits in 20 games, and he played 24.9 minutes in Saturday's win over Los Angeles, his most in the last ten games.

His three points undersell how the ice has tilted with him on it. Calgary has taken 52% of the shot attempts at five on five with him out there and 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), close to the team's level without him. But the Flames have scored 5.9 fewer goals than those chances deserve while he plays, and that kind of gap usually swings back. The caution comes from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level, and our own numbers see little offense of his own (0.36 expected goals all season). He is a steady, heavy-minute defender whose on-ice results have been unlucky so far, not a hidden scorer.
headline: Zach Whitecloud logs big minutes behind unlucky results
